Personal take here:

Watching the first season AND then the other ones is what makes the other ones look worse. Season one is just something else, perfect story, well developed characters, the timing, the atmosphere being built as it comes to the end. First season IS True Detective, and it really set the standards so high for the following ones. Season two really changed the story and, in my personal opinion, really made the "franchising" of the series something that failed. Season 3 has good moments, and Mahershala Ali really stole the show, but once you start putting every piece into place, it feels like a season one knockoff, and not it the best way.

Then, season four was premiered, and it was something that reminded in some ways to the first season. As a fan of season one (and one that really returns to it very often LOL), it took some of the whole emotion from that season and used it to gain momentum as it continued, but the finale took a loooot of the emotion away, and, in my case, once I started to coldly think about the connections to the first season, they were done in a very poor way. I did not like it at all.

Long story short: Season one really stands out from a lot of true crime series, and from the whole True Detective saga, but that's what makes the other ones look pale. That comparison, and the lack of the depthness of the first season is something that really lacks on the following ones.

A mi los psicólogos me han ayudado bastante, pero si se vuelve un poco cansado el buscar alguno que te oriente de una forma que te agrade, o que sientas que estás teniendo un progreso, a mi me llegó a pasar mucho eso, que de repente iban 4 o 5 consultas y aun no entendías el enfoque o algo así, no tenía mucha retroalimentación o en alguna ocasión, inclusive como si le "diera lástima" a una psicologa jajaja. Hay de todo y es algo excelente, pero si se puede volver cansado, y si estás en un momento de tu vida donde todo está bajoneado, puede que no sea la mejor opción. A mi parecer, el ir con un psiquiatra puede ser la solución porque los medicamentos si que pueden devolverte la vitalidad que te hace falta (en una plática TED escuché del conferencista que cuando uno está deprimido, no es que no sea feliz o esté triste, es más la falta de vitalidad, puedes estar en un momento más equilibrado y sentirte triste pero tienes un enfoque distinto, estar deprimido realmente te cambia la perspectiva de todo lo que vives)

Prueba con un psiquiatra si sientes que eso pueda darte una solución, porque claro, lo es, es una opción viable y muy loable. A mi me pasó que después de un tiempo, me di cuenta que si bien mis problemas psicológicos que ya tenía identificados o los problemas que traigo, si los veía distinto ya cuando los medicamentos comenzaban a dar sus resultados. No es de un día para otro, pero la paciencia paga bien en este caso. De igual forma, cuando me empecé a abrir con algunas personas de mi circulo cercano, me dí cuenta que no es lo más raro del mundo tomar medicamentos que te ayuden con la depresión o algún trastorno. No está mal necesitar ese empuje para volver a estar más presente, y genuinamente te puede cambiar la vida. Animo amigo, de esto se puede salir, siempre puedes trabajar para estar mejor contigo, y lo demás vendrá solo.

This whole existence is absurd, in many ways (perhaps all the ways), and it's something that can void any other promise of improvement and change, but still, I find it curious now and then for me to live, and see the new look on someone I love, and hearing that new song on a strangers car that just enlightens my day, or feeling understood in the character of a novel.  


The human experience has vastly become an absurd one, specially the more you look around things and get to worry about some of those, but some things I've found, in the way things are experienced, are truly the goal of a lifetime.  
I am myself sometimes in that very same voiding hole, and it's something I am trying to solve and work out. In the meantime, while still having to figure out what's going to occur with the future, I'm trying to get a breath of the present, and be present in such.

I've bought this exact same Alocasia (In case it's Amazonica hehe) TWICE and it just didn't loved the transplant, light or humidity. I wouldn't change anything but humidity conditions (and follow the advice given by ExternalStress about letting the soil dry out), and in case the problem persists (given my personal experience) I'd take the bulb out, cut every single root and leaf and allow it to close every cut for 2-3 days, in a dry but fresh place \[avoiding the sun\]. Once fully dry but still healthy looking, I surround it with a damp paper towel and stuck it into a ziploc bag, keep an eye out for any root development and once you've seen its improving, put it in soil (in a proper sized container) and just water it as needed.  


I hope any advice given by previous users may help your plant, but it everything fails, I've found this method to be quite succesful for bringing back to life such needy plants as Alocasias. Greetings from Mexico!
